name: Collabora Online
tagline: LibreOffice in the browser, built for self-hosting
description: An online office suite built on LibreOffice technology. It adds real-time co-editing in the browser to a file platform, and is what ships as Nextcloud Office. Desktop and mobile apps share the same engine.
licenseNote: CODE, the free Collabora Online Development Edition, is fully functional but unsupported and intended for home and small-team use. Supported, long-term builds are a paid subscription.
backing: Collabora Productivity (UK), the largest corporate contributor to LibreOffice, funded by support subscriptions

maturity.rationale: In production at large public-sector deployments and the default office editor for Nextcloud. Documents are rendered on the server, which is robust but can feel heavier than editors that run entirely in the browser.

selfHosting.summary: One container next to your file platform. Nextcloud All-in-One installs and wires it up for you; on its own you need a reverse proxy that passes WebSockets and the right allowed-host settings.

requirements.notes: Memory and CPU scale with the number of documents open at the same time.

deploy.label: CODE: Docker image and Linux packages

strengths: Fully open source, with no user or connection cap in the code
Native OpenDocument support and LibreOffice's very broad format coverage
Tight Nextcloud integration: it is the editor behind Nextcloud Office
Same engine as LibreOffice on the desktop, so documents look identical in both
weaknesses: Microsoft-format fidelity is LibreOffice's: good, not perfect
Server-rendered editing can feel laggy on a slow connection or an under-powered server
CODE builds come without support; a supported version means a subscription
Like any online editor, it needs a file platform in front of it
